newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to seek info on Elf Aquitaine's Leuna refinery.
newsitem.headline: EU to seek info on Elf Aquitaine's Leuna refinery.

text.p: The European Commission is expected to open proceedings shortly forcing Germany to provide information on subsidies paid to French oil company Elf Aquitaine to build a refinery in Leuna, east Germany.
The decision was due to be adopted at the Commission's weekly briefing later on Tuesday, but was postponed, Commission sources said. It was not immediately clear why it was delayed and for how long.

The Commission has been pressing the German authorities informally for some time to provide detailed information on the investment cost amid allegations that Elf may have inflated the price to win larger subsidies from Germany.

BvS, the successor to the Treuhand German privatisation agency, has been reported in the German press as having calculated that the work should have cost 1.96 billion marks while Elf said it was worth 3.26 billion marks.
A Commission source said the decision to start proceedings, which gives Germany a strict deadline to provide information and allows rival firms to comment, was not controversial.
